description: Schema-driven visibility and editability inside the Svelte 5 data grid. Each column carries declarative when rules evaluated against the row's current values: an EIN cell only appears on nonprofits, an SSN only on individuals, and a rejection reason only when the status is rejected. Cells that fail a visible rule are hidden, cells that fail an editable rule are locked with a contextual reason, all built on SvGrid's per-cell editable function.
keywords: svelte table hide cell by rule

faq.question: How do I make a cell editable only under some condition?
faq.answer: SvGrid accepts editable as a function of the cell context, so you can return false when the row's status is not pending. This demo wraps that in a declarative when rule so the condition lives in the schema rather than in code.

faq.question: How is a cell hidden for some rows?
faq.answer: The column's cell snippet checks the visible rule against the row and renders nothing when it fails, while the same column shows its value on rows where the rule passes.

faq.question: Why a declarative schema instead of inline checks?
faq.answer: Rules in data can be edited by people who do not touch the rendering code, combined in arrays, and reused for the reason text the locked cell shows.
